title: Layer 6 Corticothalamic Cells
intro: Layer 6 is the deepest cortical layer and the least understood. Its signature cells, corticothalamic (CT) pyramidal neurons, send feedback to the very thalamic nucleus that feeds the column, outnumbering the thalamic axons coming up by about ten to one. They do not drive the thalamus so much as tune it, and they also reach back into layer 4. Layer 6 also contains intratelencephalic cells, and a thin layer 6b at the bottom.

items: Morphology: small to medium pyramidal cells with a short apical dendrite that usually ends in layer 4 or lower layer 2/3 rather than layer 1 (Thomson 2010). Layer 6 IT cells are more varied, including inverted and horizontally oriented pyramids.

Outputs of CT cells: to the first-order thalamic nucleus of the same modality (for example the LGN for V1, VPM for barrel cortex), with a collateral to the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN), and axon branches back up to layer 4 and within layer 6. Synapses onto thalamic relay cells are on distal dendrites, are individually weak, facilitate with repeated activity and act partly through metabotropic glutamate receptors. These are the hallmarks of 'modulator' rather than 'driver' input (Sherman & Guillery 1998).
Inputs: thalamus (layer 6 also receives thalamic axon branches), layer 4 and layer 5 cells, and long-range cortical input.

Firing: regular spiking. In vivo many CT cells are remarkably quiet, firing little in response to sensory stimulation unless the animal is active or the stimulus is in a particular state (Velez-Fort et al. 2014 in mouse V1; Kwegyir-Afful & Simons 2009 in barrel cortex).

Effect on the circuit: optogenetically driving layer 6 CT cells in mouse V1 scales down activity in all the other layers without changing what the cells prefer, a gain control mediated by translaminar fast-spiking interneurons in layer 6 (Olsen et al. 2012; Bortone et al. 2014). On the thalamus they can enhance or suppress depending on firing rate, because they excite relay cells directly and inhibit them via the TRN (Crandall et al. 2015).
Gain control and attention: CT feedback adjusts how strongly the thalamus relays input and whether relay cells are in tonic or burst mode.
Sharpening receptive fields: CT feedback can synchronise and focus thalamic responses on features the cortex is processing (Sillito et al. 2006).

Location and motor signals in the Thousand Brains Theory: Hawkins et al. (2019) and Lewis et al. (2019) propose that layer 6 represents the location of the sensor in an object's reference frame, using grid-cell-like codes, and passes that location to layer 4 as context. Layer 6a projects to layer 4, and layer 6 receives motor-related input, which fits this role, but the specific grid-cell hypothesis is not yet tested.
Detailed: Blue Brain's L6 m-types (L6_TPC_L1, L6_TPC_L4, L6_UTPC, L6_IPC, L6_BPC) with fitted e-types; the Allen Institute's biophysical and GLIF models of mouse layer 6 CT cells.
Point neurons: regular-spiking LIF, AdEx or Izhikevich cells. Potjans-Diesmann layer 6 has about 14,400 excitatory LIF cells.

Thalamocortical loop models: Destexhe, Contreras and Steriade (1998) and Bazhenov et al. (2002) used corticothalamic feedback in conductance-based models of spindle and slow-wave oscillations; Traub et al. (2005) built a single-column thalamocortical model with layer 6 CT cells and thalamus; Izhikevich and Edelman (2008) included layer 6 CT projections in a large-scale thalamocortical model.

Thousand Brains / HTM: layer 6 is modelled as grid-cell modules plus a sensory-location layer feeding layer 4's distal dendrites (see Reference Frames, #/computational-cortical-columns/thousand-brains/reference-frames).

blocks.text: What this means for your SNN

items: If your column has a model thalamus, close the loop: layer 6 → thalamic relay (weak, facilitating, modulatory) and layer 6 → TRN → relay (inhibitory).
Treat layer 6 output to layer 4 as modulatory context, not driving input, for example as input to a distal or apical compartment.
Use layer 6 as the natural home for a location signal if you are following the Thousand Brains architecture.
Keep layer 6 rates low; its influence comes from many weak synapses and facilitation, not from strong single connections.
